questions.statement: Which adverb of frequency means "0% of the time"?

options.feedback: Incorrect. "Always" means 100% of the time.
Incorrect. "Sometimes" means about 50% of the time.
Correct! "Never" indicates that an action does not happen at all.
Incorrect. "Often" means frequently.

questions.explanation:
The student identifies the basic meaning of the adverb "never".

questions.statement:
What is the correct position for the adverb "usually" in this sentence?
"I ________ eat breakfast at 6:30 AM."

options.feedback: Correct! Adverbs of frequency normally go before the main verb.
Incorrect. The adverb should come before the verb "eat".
Incorrect. While possible in some contexts, the standard position is between subject and verb.
Incorrect. This is not the standard position for this adverb.

questions.explanation:
The student remembers the standard placement of frequency adverbs in relation to the main verb.

questions.statement:
Valentina: "How often do you go to the park on Sundays?"
Mateo: "________________________"
questions.context: A conversation about weekend activities in Colombia.

options.feedback: Incorrect. This answers "With whom?" not "How often?".

options.text: I always go in the afternoon.
options.feedback: Correct! This answers the frequency question using "always".
Incorrect. This answers a "Do you...?" question, not a "How often...?" question.
Incorrect. This is a description, not a frequency response.

questions.explanation:
The student understands how to respond to a "How often" question using frequency adverbs.

questions.context: Using the verb "to be" with frequency adverbs.

options.feedback: Incorrect. Adverbs of frequency go AFTER the verb "to be".
Correct! With the verb "to be", the adverb follows the verb.
Incorrect. This is not the natural word order.
Incorrect. This is less common and less natural than placing the adverb after the verb.

The student understands the specific rule for frequency adverbs used with the verb "to be".

questions.statement: "My brother is very responsible. He ________ late for school."

options.feedback: Correct! Being responsible implies he is not late, and "is" comes before "never".
Incorrect. Word order error: with "to be", the adverb comes after.
Incorrect. "Always late" contradicts "very responsible".
Incorrect. Wrong word order and wrong meaning for the context.

The student applies grammatical rules and contextual logic to choose the correct adverb and position.

questions.statement: How often does the family cook on Sundays?
questions.context:
A short description of a family's habits.
"On weekdays, we usually have dinner at home. However, on Saturdays, we often go to a restaurant. We never cook on Sundays."

options.feedback: Incorrect. The text says they usually eat at home on weekdays.
Incorrect. "Often" refers to their Saturday restaurant visits.
Incorrect. The text uses a stronger negative adverb.
Correct! The text explicitly states "We never cook on Sundays."

questions.explanation:
The student applies reading strategies to identify specific frequency information in a text.

options.feedback: Incorrect. This would mean only one day.

questions.subject: ingles

questions.statement: Which statement about Sara is true?
questions.context:
Analyzing a schedule.
"Sara: Gym (Mon, Tue, Wed, Thu, Fri) / English (Sat) / Cinema (Once a month)"

options.text: She always goes to the gym.
options.feedback: Incorrect. "Always" would mean every day, including weekends. She goes on weekdays.

options.text: She often goes to the gym.
options.feedback: Correct! Five times a week is a high frequency, described well by "often" or "usually".

options.text: She never goes to the cinema.
options.feedback: Incorrect. She goes once a month.

options.text: She goes to English class every day.
options.feedback: Incorrect. She only goes on Saturdays.

questions.explanation:
The student analyzes a schedule to determine which frequency adverb or expression accurately describes the behavior.

questions.subject: ingles

questions.context: Comparing frequency adverbs in a sentence.

options.text: I never brush my teeth, so they are very clean.
options.feedback: Incorrect. If you never brush them, they won't be clean.

options.text: I always study for tests, so I usually fail them.
options.feedback: Incorrect. Studying usually leads to passing, not failing.

options.text: I sometimes forget my umbrella, so I get wet when it rains.
options.feedback: Correct! This is a logical cause-and-effect relationship using "sometimes".

options.text: I usually wake up at 5:00 AM, so I am often late for my 7:00 AM class.
options.feedback: Incorrect. Waking up at 5:00 for a 7:00 class is plenty of time; you wouldn't be late.

questions.explanation:
The student analyzes the logical consistency of sentences containing frequency adverbs.

questions.statement: Based on the text, what is the main reason Lucas is the best student?
questions.context:
A paragraph about a student's dedication.
"Lucas is the best student in class. He always finishes his homework, he is never late, and he often asks interesting questions. He usually studies at the library after school."

options.text: Because he goes to the library every day.
options.feedback: Incorrect. The text says he "usually" goes, not every day.

options.text: Because he is never late to class.
options.feedback: Incorrect. This is just one of his good habits, not the only reason.

options.text: Because he consistently maintains several good academic habits.
options.feedback: Correct! The text lists multiple positive behaviors (always finishing homework, being on time, asking questions, studying).

options.text: Because he asks questions once in a while.
options.feedback: Incorrect. The text says "often", which is more frequent than "once in a while".

questions.explanation: The student evaluates the cumulative information in the text to identify the most comprehensive conclusion.
